title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account. From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can select cryptographic groups from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our getting started page .

This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools. AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
summary: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations. With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account. title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs. To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. summary: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin. With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types. title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
summary: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second. With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover. To learn more, see the Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page . For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the AWS Regional Services page .

The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal. With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you. With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%. Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection. Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage. With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually. Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language. Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. summary: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API
summary: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications. Customers can configure application load balancing using Gateway and HTTPRoute resources, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS infrastructure automatically. With this launch, EKS Auto Mode customers can adopt the next-generation Kubernetes traffic management standard without installing or configuring a separate controller. Capabilities include HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace traffic routing for multi-team environments, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager. Existing workloads using Ingress resources continue to work alongside Gateway API resources. To get started, see the Amazon EKS documentation . Gateway API support is included as part of EKS Auto Mode and is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported.

summary: AWS Backup restore testing now supports Amazon Redshift. You can now include Amazon Redshift in your restore testing plans alongside other supported AWS resources across storage, compute, and database services. Organizations can now give their teams one curated catalog that puts software, data, and AI tools from AWS Marketplace alongside physical goods and supplies from Amazon Business. Many enterprises already buy from both, but they manage two catalogs with duplicated approval rules and separate reporting. The unified storefront can now give procurement teams one front door for both. Built on AWS Marketplace Storefront, the unified storefront lets administrators connect their organization's Amazon Business account and import Amazon Business products into their branded storefront. summary: Amazon SageMaker AI MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, bringing a redesigned tracing experience and faster experiment tracking to your generative AI and machine learning workflows. MLflow 3.16 improves debugging and analysis of generative AI applications and agents. The redesigned trace explorer is now the default, with adjustable row height, reorderable columns, custom columns from any trace tag or metadata field. This release also accelerates metric charts for experiments with large metric histories. New MLflow Apps are created on MLflow 3.16 by default. Existing MLflow Apps will be upgraded to MLflow 3.16 during an upcoming maintenance window, with no action required. MLflow 3.16 is available in all AWS Regions where MLflow Apps are available. summary: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use. With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. summary: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey data tiering is now available on Graviton4-based R8gd nodes in the AWS Europe (Spain) Region, and on Graviton3-based R7gd nodes in the Europe (Spain) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) Regions. Data tiering is a lower-cost way to scale your Valkey clusters to hundreds of terabytes of capacity. It uses solid state drives (SSDs) on each node alongside memory. When memory fills up, ElastiCache automatically moves the least recently used items to SSD. When your application reads an item stored on SSD, ElastiCache moves it back into memory before serving the request. Data tiering is a good fit for workloads that regularly access up to 20% of their dataset, and for applications that can tolerate some extra latency when they read data from SSD. title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now supports changing durability on existing clusters
summary: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters. Previously, you couldn't change the durability configuration of an existing cluster in place. This made it harder to move from caching to persistent data store use cases, or to adapt as your application requirements change. Now you can change durability at any point in your application's lifecycle. You can choose between two durability options: synchronous and asynchronous writes. Synchronous writes persist data across at least two AZs before responding to the client, designed for zero data loss at single-digit millisecond write latency. Asynchronous writes persist data after responding to the client, maintaining microsecond write latency at no additional cost. However, up to 10 seconds of uncommitted data could be lost in the rare event of a failure. Both options maintain microsecond read latency. title: Amazon Neptune now supports online index rebuild to reclaim storage
summary: Amazon Neptune Database now supports online index rebuild, a new capability that helps database administrators and application teams defragment Neptune indexes and reclaim unused storage space without taking their database offline. Over time, insert, update, and delete operations create gaps of unused space within data pages, keeping the VolumeBytesUsed metric artificially elevated even after data is deleted. This fragmentation increases I/O costs and degrades query performance for teams running Gremlin, openCypher, or SPARQL workloads at scale. With online index rebuild, read and write queries continue uninterrupted on both the writer instance and read replicas throughout the entire rebuild process. You can target all indexes, only quad indexes, or only dictionary indexes, making this feature well-suited for post-deletion cleanup, periodic maintenance, storage limit management, and performance tuning on heavily fragmented databases. title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
summary: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destinations with a single API call. Replication backfill is useful when expanding to a new AWS Region, validating disaster recovery readiness, updating replication rules, or ensuring complete image catalogs exist across Regions for compliance purposes. summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports the ModifyVolume API, which lets you change volume size, volume type, IOPS, or throughput in place, without detaching the volume or restarting the instance. Instead of a buffering wheel or frozen frame, viewers see the slate until the broadcaster reconnects. Live playback then resumes automatically, without viewers needing to refresh their player. The failover slate helps you retain your audience during momentary disruptions and is ideal for broadcasters streaming from mobile devices or from locations with unreliable connectivity. You can enable the failover slate on new or existing channels and monitor slate activity with Amazon EventBridge events and Amazon CloudWatch metrics. With this launch, customers can set this visual preference in both IAM-based and IDC-based domains. See how any metric differs for repeat callers versus the rest of your contacts, or how results hold up among your highest-LTV customers; so you can spot the groups trending the wrong way before it shows up in the aggregate. You can now see whether an interaction worked, not just how efficiently it ran. title: AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
summary: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), a post-quantum cryptography standard under NIST FIPS 203 , which enables two parties to establish a shared secret. NIST designed ML-KEM to replace the classical key-establishment schemes, like DH/ECDH key agreement, and RSA-based key transport, in their strategic cryptographic roadmap (see NIST IR 8547 ). ML-KEM addresses the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat to those classical schemes, where an adversary records the key-establishment exchange today and recovers the shared secret once sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available. KMS supports all three ML-KEM key specs defined in NIST FIPS 203: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. The Encapsulate API uses the public key to produce a random 32-byte shared secret and its ciphertext form. title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation
summary: Trusted identity propagation carries a user's identity with their request, so AWS services can grant permissions based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and log that user's access for auditing. Customers often distribute workloads across AWS Regions for many reasons including separating the compute from the data it queries, to running workloads where capacity is available, or for disaster recovery and global scale. Previously, trusted identity propagation required all of the AWS services accessing a user's identity to reside in the same AWS Region. title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances
summary: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you enable Launch Before Terminate as the default replacement behavior across all Auto Scaling groups in your account. When enabled, Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating the instance it replaces, helping your applications maintain full capacity and availability during instance replacement events. This applies to replacement events such as instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks, and maximum-instance-lifetime replacements. title: CVE-2026-109587 & CVE-2026-109588 - Issue with FreeRTOS-Kernel
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-138-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/16/2026 10:00 AM PDT Description: FreeRTOS-Kernel is a real-time operating system kernel for microcontrollers and small microprocessors, distributed by Amazon. AWS identified two issues with the FreeRTOS-Kernel Arm Cortex-R82 (Armv8-R AArch64) MPU port, affecting multiple versions. CVE-2026-109587: incorrect authorization in the Arm Cortex-R82 MPU port. On MPU-enabled builds, the port does not correctly enforce the memory-region boundaries assigned to an unprivileged task when it passes a buffer argument to an MPU system call. Under certain conditions, an unprivileged task might read and write privileged kernel memory outside the regions assigned to it. This issue affects Arm Cortex-R82 builds with configENABLE_MPU=1; applications that do not use the FreeRTOS MPU are not affected. CVE-2026-109588: numeric truncation in the MPU buffer authorization check on the Arm Cortex-R82 MPU port.

summary: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre filtering, delivering up to 5x higher recall on filtered searches. Filters evaluate before similarity search so scoped queries return more relevant results. Ideal for RAG, agentic apps, and document search.

title: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL now supports direct querying of Apache Iceberg and Parquet data in your data lake
summary: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL now lets you directly query Apache Iceberg and Parquet data stored in your data lake alongside live operational data—no ETL pipelines required. Powered by DuckDB embedded within Aurora, this capability enables single queries that join transactional and historical data using familiar PostgreSQL syntax. It supports AWS Glue Data Catalog, S3, and S3 Tables, with optimizations like predicate pushdown and caching for efficient performance.

title: Introducing enhanced custom event buses in Amazon EventBridge for enterprise-scale event-driven applications
summary: Amazon EventBridge announces an enhanced custom event bus for organizations scaling event-driven applications across teams and accounts. Deploy a single event bus shared across all AWS accounts in your organization, with ordering guarantees, a simplified Subscriber resource, and improved economics at scale.

title: CVE-2026-95985 - Kiro IDE Allows Agentic Writes to Global Configurations While Working in Untrusted Workspaces
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-117-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 09/24/2026 10:00 AM PDT Description: Kiro is an agentic IDE that users install on their desktop. We identified CVE-2026-95985. The file write tool in Kiro IDE before version 1.0.242 might allow remote unauthenticated actors to execute arbitrary commands and to inject crafted instructions into the agent's context. When a user runs the agent in a crafted repository as an untrusted workspace, sending any message can cause agent modifications to auto-loaded global configuration paths. Impacted versions: < 1.0.242 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin. View article

summary: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is the next evolution of CloudWatch — unified observability that brings your applications and AI agents into one reimagined experience, with auto-discovered topology, natural language queries, and AI-guided investigation powered by AWS DevOps Agent.

title: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch Omni: AI-powered observability for generative AI and agentic workloads
summary: Learn how Amazon CloudWatch Omni delivers AI-powered observability purpose-built for generative AI and agentic workloads. Trace, evaluate, and experiment with AI agents across any framework—directly from your IDE or a standalone web experience—using open standards and built-in evaluators for quality, correctness, and coherence.

title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
summary: AWS introduces new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (Granite Rapids), available only on AWS. T8i instances are among the lowest-cost EC2 instances and deliver up to 30% better price performance over previous generation T3 instances.

title: AWS Elastic Beanstalk introduces Cluster Mode
summary: Run an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk Cluster Mode without provisioning or operating the compute underneath it. You provide a container image or source code; Elastic Beanstalk with service-operated compute creates and operates the environment that runs it.
